# **Comprehensive Crawler Target Guide for Discovering A2A Agent Cards**

To build a high-recall crawler for Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol Agent Cards, you cannot rely solely on scanning domain roots for the canonical /.well-known/agent-card.json path1. While the Linux Foundation's A2A v1.0.0 specification (which reached v1.0.0 on March 12, 2026\) standardizes discovery around RFC 8615 well-known URIs, ecosystem data shows that live Agent Cards are distributed across legacy URI paths, multi-agent manifests, public aggregator APIs, recursive "directory-of-directories" agents, Ethereum smart contracts (ERC-8004), federated OCI/DNS registries, and enterprise cloud catalogs2. In a July 2026 probe of 22,341 web domains reported by API Evangelist, 65 domains hosted an Agent Card at the domain level; of those, 23.1% (15 domains, including Cloudflare) still served their cards at the deprecated /.well-known/agent.json path where strict v1.0.0 clients do not look, and 15.4% (10 domains) were fully spec-conformant2.  
Consequently, maximizing discovery yield requires a multi-tiered harvesting architecture that combines **direct HTTP path probing** with **structured registry ingestion** and **protocol-level spidering**2. The highest-yield immediate targets are public registry APIs—such as allagents.app (which reports 14,079 listed agents in its registry card), a2aregistry.org (tracking 690 registered agents, with 676 reachable as of its November 12, 2026 sweep), and www\.a2a-registry.org—alongside on-chain ERC-8004 identity indexers (8004scan.io, agentscan.info, 8004agents.ai) and the 114 meta-directory agents indexed on a2aregistry.org that expose their own downstream catalogs via A2A message/send or Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoints7. Beyond these core hubs, standards tracking by AgentProbe across the IETF, Linux Foundation, W3C, MIT, Ethereum, and OWASP reveals **63 active specifications, drafts, and charters** proposing **33 distinct discovery mechanisms** and claiming **more than 25 well-known URI paths** alongside local mDNS (\_a2a.\_tcp.local.), WebFinger (acct: URI resolution), and unicast DNS (SVCB, AIDISCA, AIINDEX, \_agent, and \_ans-badge) records12.  
The master table below summarizes the seven primary target tiers where your crawlers should be dispatched, ordered by discovery mechanism and harvesting complexity.

| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |

Domain-Level HTTP Paths** | RFC 8615 Well-Known URIs, root manifests, and framework routes | /.well-known/agent-card.json /.well-known/agent.json /.well-known/agents.json /agents.json and /agent.json /.well-known/agent-card.json?assistant\_id={id} /a2a/.well-known/agent.json | Single A2A v1.0/v0.3 AgentCard JSON, or agents.json array of agent objects1. |

## **1\. Domain-Level HTTP Probing: Well-Known URIs, Multi-Agent Manifests, and Framework Routes**

When sending HTTP crawlers directly against a seed list of domains or subdomains, probing /.well-known/agent-card.json alone will miss nearly a quarter of deployed single-agent cards and all multi-agent manifest arrays2. Under RFC 8615, the A2A specification originally recommended /.well-known/agent.json in v0.2.444. Following an IETF well-known-uris registry review in July 2025 (Issue \#66), where reviewers noted that agent.json was overly generic for a vendor proposal, the specification maintainers renamed the canonical path to /.well-known/agent-card.json via a breaking refactor on July 29, 202545. While the official A2A Python SDK (a2a-python PR \#352) added deprecation warnings for the legacy path alongside the new one, a substantial share of early deployments still serve cards exclusively at /.well-known/agent.json45.  
Furthermore, single-file agent-card.json documents only describe a single agent object14. Because each A2A protocol version or distinct agent on a host would otherwise require its own N-level subdomain (e.g., https\://myagent-a2a-v1.0.example.org/.well-known/agent-card.json), multi-agent platforms and marketplaces have adopted agents.json array manifests at either /.well-known/agents.json or the domain root /agents.json2. Your HTTP crawler should probe the exact URI path matrix below on every target host.

| Path / Endpoint Template | Spec / Origin | Payload Structure | Real-World Examples & Crawler Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| /.well-known/agent-card.json | Official A2A v0.3 & v1.0.0 Standard (RFC 8615\) | Single AgentCard JSON object (supportedInterfaces in v1.0; top-level url in v0.3)1. | Canonical path required by strict A2A v1.0.0 clients, A2ACardResolver in Microsoft Agent Framework, and ERC-80042. |
| /.well-known/agent.json | Legacy A2A v0.2.4 & NAIS Spec | Single AgentCard JSON object2. | **Critical fallback:** 15 of 65 domains with cards in the July 2026 API Evangelist scan used this path exclusively, including https\://www\.cloudflare.com/.well-known/agent.json45. |
| /.well-known/agents.json | A2A Registry Multi-Agent Spec & Wildcard AI v0.1.0 | JSON array \[ {...}, {...} \] of agent objects (or OpenAPI-based manifest)40. | Used when a single domain hosts multiple services or team-owned agents (name, description, url, version, capabilities, openapi\_url)40. |
| /agents.json | Top-Level Domain Agent Index | JSON object containing an "agents": \[...\] pointer array45. | Used in production by Cloudflare at https\://www\.cloudflare.com/agents.json to index its protocol: "a2a" card URL45. |
| /agent.json & /agent-card.json | Agent Web Protocol (www\.agent-json.org) & Root Card Deployments | Root-level agent descriptor JSON or A2A v1.0 AgentCard2. | Flagged by AI readiness checkers (okfor.ai/checks/agent-json); also used in production by live A2A v1.0 agents such as https\://mydanktank.com/agent-card.json2. |
| /.well-known/agent-card.json?assistant\_id={id} | LangGraph / LangSmith Agent Server (langgraph-api\>=0.4.21) | Single AgentCard JSON dynamically generated per LangGraph assistant16. | LangGraph deployments multiplex multiple assistants behind one server; requires discovering or enumerating assistant\_id values16. |
| /a2a/.well-known/agent.json | OpenAgents Network (openagents.org) | Single AgentCard JSON aggregating skills across network mods15. | Default OpenAgents HTTP transport runs on port 8700 with /a2a prefix; also supports JSON-RPC agents/list on POST /a2a11. |
| /.wellknown/agent-card.json | AgentScope Runtime Config Default | Single AgentCard JSON (typically on default port 8080\)29. | Documented default string in agentscope\_runtime (AgentCardWithRuntimeConfig) omits the hyphen in wellknown2. |
| /runtimes/{escaped\_arn}/invocations/.well-known/agent-card.json | AWS Bedrock AgentCore Runtime | Hybrid A2A v0.3/v1.0 AgentCard JSON (includes both supportedInterfaces and top-level url)28. | Hosted on bedrock-agentcore.{region}.amazonaws.com; requires X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id header and AWS SigV4 GetAgentCard IAM action28. |
| /adb/a2a/v1/databases/{db-ocid}/agents/{team}/.well-known/agent-card.json | Oracle Cloud Autonomous AI Database (Select AI) | Single AgentCard JSON mapped from Select AI agent teams43. | Hosted on dataaccess.adb.{region-identifier}.oraclecloudapps.com; requires Authorization: Bearer {token}43. |
| /api/v1/a2a/agents/{group\_id}/.well-known/agent-card.json | Nanonets Agent Marketplaces (A2A v1.0) | Single A2A v1.0 AgentCard JSON using JSON-RPC binding10. | {group\_id} persists across publishes; authenticates via X-API-Key (marketplace key) or Authorization: Bearer10. |
| /a2a/{service-slug}/.well-known/agent-card.json | Enterprise API Gateway Sub-Path Mounting (e.g., CDQ Genius) | Single AgentCard JSON mounted beneath an API gateway prefix50. | Exemplified by CDQ Genius at https\://api.cdq.com/a2a/cdq-genius/.well-known/agent-card.json where JSON-RPC calls POST to /a2a/cdq-genius/50. |
| /a2a/agent/authenticatedExtendedCard | A2A Extended Agent Card REST Endpoint | Full authenticated AgentCard JSON with private/gated skills44. | Invoked via GET with Authorization: Bearer {token} after a public card declares extendedAgentCard: true1. |

### **Expanded Well-Known URI Matrix: 27+ Paths Claimed Across 63 Agent Discovery Standards**

According to the AgentProbe Standards tracker (agentprobe.org/standards), there are currently **63 specifications, Internet-Drafts, and working group charters** (46 at the IETF, 6 at the Linux Foundation, 5 at the W3C, 2 Community specs, and 1 each from Google, Ethereum, MIT, and OWASP) proposing 33 discovery mechanisms13. Several of these specifications define container catalogs or cross-protocol manifests that directly embed, inline, or link to A2A Agent Cards. To ensure your HTTP crawlers capture A2A cards wrapped inside broader discovery envelopes, add the following secondary well-known paths to your domain scanner:

| Well-Known Path / Endpoint | Governing Spec(s) & Standards Body | How It Exposes or Links to A2A Agent Cards |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| /.well-known/ai-catalog.json | Linux Foundation lf-ai-catalog, Google google-ard, draft-mp-agntcy-ads, draft-raskar-agentic-web-federated-resolution, mcp-server-cards | A typed, nestable JSON container that inlines or references A2A Agent Cards (application/a2a+json), MCP servers, model cards, and sub-catalogs alongside did:web publisher identities and signed Trust Manifests13. Validated natively by **Google Lighthouse 13.5+** audits in Chrome DevTools and PageSpeed Insights13. |
| /.well-known/ard.json & GET /agents | Agentic Resource Discovery (google-ard v0.91 / IETF draft-bu-dawn-ard-discovery) | JSON-LD node (urn:air identifiers) cataloging A2A agents, MCP tools, and skills; falls back to /.well-known/ai-catalog.json and exposes a cacheable GET /agents?pageSize=\&pageToken=\&filter= deterministic list endpoint13. |
| /.well-known/webfinger?resource=acct:{name}@{domain} | IETF draft-zhao-a2a-webfinger-00 (WebFinger Profile for A2A) | Solves multi-agent hosting on a single domain without N-level subdomains13. Returns a JSON Resource Descriptor (JRD) whose links\[\] array contains {"rel": "self", "type": "application/a2a+json", "href": "https\://.../.well-known/agent-card.json"}13. |
| /.well-known/agents.txt & /agents.txt | IETF draft-car-agents-txt-wellknown & draft-srijal-agents-policy | Block-based plaintext capability declaration (paired with /.well-known/agents.json via Agents-JSON:) where Capability blocks explicitly declare Protocol: A2A and Endpoint: https\://...13. |
| /.well-known/agent-registration.json | Ethereum ERC-8004 (Trustless Agents) | Published on an agent's HTTPS domain to prove domain ownership by linking the web origin back to its on-chain registrations (agentId and agentRegistry CAIP-10 identifier)13. |
| /.well-known/ad | IETF draft-jimenez-agent-directory (Ericsson) & draft-zhang-dawn-agent-discovery-framework | Adapts CoRE Resource Directory (RFC 9176\) to HTTP/JSON, aggregating per-agent metadata into a single queryable lookup endpoint so clients need not poll individual /.well-known/agent-card.json files13. |
| /.well-known/agent | IETF draft-nemethi-aid-agent-identity-discovery & draft-nemethi-dawn-aid (AID v1.2 / v2) | Well-known endpoint paired with \_agent.\<domain\> DNS TXT lookups for lightweight protocol token and endpoint resolution prior to A2A handshake13. |
| /.well-known/agent-descriptions | W3C w3c-ai-agent-protocol-cg (Agent Network Protocol / ANP) | Publishes JSON-LD and W3C DID-anchored agent descriptions for cross-domain discovery and role negotiation13. |
| /.well-known/ans/trust-card.json | IETF draft-narajala-courtney-ansv2 (GoDaddy / OWASP / Cisco ANS v2) | Domain-anchored trust metadata binding an agent's ANSName (ans://v{version}.{agentHost}) to transparency log receipts and X.509 certificates13. |
| /.well-known/signature-agent-card & /.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory | IETF draft-meunier-webbotauth-registry & draft-ietf-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol (Cloudflare / Google / Amazon) | Publishes a "Signature Agent Card" (OAuth DCR/CIMD parameters \+ web\_bot\_auth object with trigger, purpose, jwks\_uri) for automated HTTP clients using RFC 9421 message signatures13. |
| /.well-known/ains/ (GET /resolve/{name} & GET /lookup) | IETF draft-vandemeent-ains-discovery (AInternet Name Service) | Resolves .aint / .waint / .raint agent names (Content-Type: application/ains+json) and supports capability lookups (GET {prefix}/lookup?capability={cap}) with TIBET/UPIP provenance anchors13. |
| /.well-known/ardp/query & /.well-known/ardp/resolve | IETF draft-pioli-agent-discovery (Agent Registration & Discovery Protocol) | Federated control plane exposing /register, /deregister, /resolve, /query, /meta, and /nonce for agents advertising A2A, MCP, HTTP, or gRPC capabilities13. |
| /.well-known/agis/id/ & /agents/{agent}.json | IETF draft-ayoub-agis-agent-identity-system | Per-agent JSON identity, JWKS (/agents/{agent}/jwks.json), and live status (/agents/{agent}/status.json) endpoints13. |
| /.well-known/proof.json | IETF draft-raskar-agentic-web-federated-resolution (MIT NANDA) | Verifiable authority proof file binding split-hosted or non-DNS publishers to terminal A2A Agent Cards or subject-authorized gateways13. |
| /llms.txt & /llms-full.txt | Community llms-txt Spec (llmstxt.org) | Markdown index of machine-readable site files; frequently linked directly inside read-only A2A Agent Cards (such as Cloudflare's site-context skill)2. |

### **Extracting Hidden Skills via GetExtendedAgentCard**

Public Agent Cards found at well-known URIs frequently omit sensitive or proprietary capabilities1. When your crawler parses a public card, inspect capabilities.extendedAgentCard (in A2A v1.0) or capabilities.supportsAuthenticatedExtendedCard (in A2A v0.3)1. When this boolean is true, the server exposes a fuller card via the GetExtendedAgentCard operation (or agent/getAuthenticatedExtendedCard in v0.3, and GET /a2a/agent/authenticatedExtendedCard over HTTP REST)1. If your crawler holds valid out-of-band credentials (or if the server uses a permissive or free registration flow declared in securitySchemes), invoking this method returns the extended Agent Card containing additional skills and execution settings not shown in the public card1.

## **2\. Public A2A Registries and Primary Aggregator APIs**

Rather than scanning thousands of cold domains—where the empirical hit rate in the July 2026 API Evangelist probe was roughly 0.29% (65 out of 22,341 domains)—your highest-efficiency starting point is ingesting existing public A2A registries45. The ecosystem currently features seven distinct public registry and marketplace platforms that expose programmatic REST APIs, bulk JSON dumps, Meta Agent RPC endpoints, or MCP interfaces.  
![][image2]

### **1\. a2aregistry.org (Open-Source Live Agent Registry)**

Maintained by Prassanna Ravishankar (github.com/prassanna-ravishankar/a2a-registry), a2aregistry.org indexes live, hosted A2A agents rather than static code repositories7. As of its November 12, 2026 sweep (12:28 UTC), it tracks **690 registered agents, with 676 verified reachable** across 20 listed category tags (up from 644 registered and 628 reachable on November 11, 2026\)11. Crucially for crawler operators, its backend worker runs daily active health and task-conformance probes (User-Agent: A2A-Registry-TaskProbe/1.0 and A2A-Registry-Smoke/1.0) by sending a real message/send request via the A2A SDK to verify whether endpoints actually respond rather than merely serving a static JSON card7.  
You can harvest a2aregistry.org through four programmatic channels:

> 1. **REST API (https\://a2aregistry.org/api & /api/openapi.json)**: Query GET https\://a2aregistry.org/api/agents to paginate the register, or filter via GET /api/agents?conformance=standard, GET /api/agents?search={keyword}, and GET /api/agents?skill={tag}, and pull aggregate counts via GET /api/stats1. Individual agent snapshots, on-demand rechecks, health checks, 30-day uptime metrics, maintainer notes, and chat proxying are available at GET /api/agents/{id}, GET /api/agents/{id}/recheck, GET /api/agents/{id}/health, GET /api/agents/{id}/uptime, PATCH /api/agents/{id}/notes, POST /api/agents/{id}/flag, and POST /api/agents/{id}/chat (interactive OAS 3.1 docs at https\://a2aregistry.org/api/docs)1.  
> 2. **Consolidated JSON Feed & GitHub Repo**: The static Git-as-a-database workflow consolidates merged pull requests into https\://www\.a2aregistry.org/registry.json, where every entry includes the canonical AgentCard fields plus author and wellKnownURI19.  
> 3. **Python Client SDK**: Install via pip install a2a-registry-client and invoke APIRegistry().get\_all() or Registry().find\_by\_skill("...") to pull all indexed records directly into a Python crawler worker17.  
> 4. **MCP Server**: Connect an MCP client to https\://a2aregistry.org/mcp/ to query the registry via tool calls.

### **2\. allagents.app (World Directory of AI Agents — 14,079 Reported Listings)**

Operated from Switzerland, allagents.app describes itself in its agent card as a world directory of AI agents by specialty with **14,079 listed agents**, daily liveness checks (alive status), and 14-day track records8. It is itself a live A2A agent (registered on a2aregistry.org under ID 4bac7ffc-c964-43e2-acbb-302beca35838) and exposes four bulk-query surfaces2:

> 1. **Canonical A2A Card & Endpoint**: Fetch https\://allagents.app/.well-known/agent-card.json and send A2A message/send requests to POST https\://allagents.app/a2a invoking the find or operator skills2.  
> 2. **Constraint Discovery REST Endpoint (POST /discover)**: Send a JSON payload to https\://allagents.app/discover with structured filters—{need, alive, protocols, endpoint, payment, country, specialty, tags, exclude, claimed, limit}—to harvest ranked agents that expressly support "a2a" and answered the daily liveness check2.  
> 3. **Keyword Search & Trust Endpoints**: Query GET https\://allagents.app/search?q={specialty} for direct listings and GET https\://allagents.app/agent/{id}/trust for verified protocol history and 14-day uptime2.  
> 4. **Stateless MCP Server (https\://allagents.app/mcp)**: Connect over Streamable HTTP (no account required to read) and invoke list\_specialties, search\_agents, and get\_agent to systematically enumerate the catalog2.

### **3\. www\.a2a-registry.org (The Global AI Agent Directory & Meta Agent)**

Distinct from a2aregistry.org (unhyphenated), https\://www\.a2a-registry.org is a public directory focused on agent-to-agent commerce, DNS-verified trust badges, GoDaddy ANS name resolution, and autonomous x402 crypto payments (USDC on Base, Solana, and Polygon)10. When developers submit a domain URL, www\.a2a-registry.org auto-discovers the domain's /.well-known/agent-card.json (assigning reverse-DNS identifiers like com.domain.{slug}), multi-agent /.well-known/agents.json manifests, GoDaddy ANS endpoints, or uploaded card files (user.{userId}.{slug})14. Crawlers can harvest www\.a2a-registry.org through four interfaces:

> 1. **Meta Agent Card (https\://www\.a2a-registry.org/.well-known/agent-card.json)**: The registry operates as a compliant A2A v1.0 Meta Agent that dynamically discovers and chains registered agents14.  
> 2. **Native A2A v1.0 JSON-RPC Discovery Endpoint**: Send POST https\://api.a2a-registry.org/a2a/v1 with a JSON-RPC payload {"method": "message/send", "params": {"query": "translate"}} to retrieve matching Agent Cards over native A2A14.  
> 3. **Direct REST Search Endpoint**: Query POST https\://api.a2a-registry.org/a2a/discover with header Authorization: Bearer zv\_YOUR\_TOKEN and JSON body {"query": "translate text", "limit": 5}14.  
> 4. **Category Web Portals**: Crawl https\://www\.a2a-registry.org/browse across its eight primary categories (Productivity, Development, Data, Content, Social, Utilities, Finance, Lifestyle, e.g., ?category=Data or ?category=Utilities)7.

### **4\. flowmarket.social/a2a-registry/ (FlowMarket B2B Industrial A2A Directory)**

FlowMarket operates a B2B network where companies deploy autonomous AI agents to represent them in commercial procurement and supplier qualification40. Its public **A2A Registry** (https\://flowmarket.social/a2a-registry/) exclusively lists active company agents that have the Agent2Agent protocol switched on and are reachable over A2A40. Crucially, each listing links to the agent's profile while the Agent Card itself lives at the company agent's own external URL, allowing A2A crawlers to fetch cards directly from supplier hosts across 16+ industrial verticals (Agriculture & Farming, Food & Beverage, Chemicals, Pharmaceuticals & Life Sciences, Metals & Metalworking, Machinery & Industrial Equipment, Automotive, Aerospace & Defense, Electronics & Electrical, Plastics & Rubber, Construction & Building Materials, Energy & Utilities, Oil, Gas & Mining, Textiles & Apparel, Furniture & Wood, and Paper & Packaging)40.

### **5\. a2aagentlist.com (Curated A2A & OpenClaw Agent Directory)**

**A2A Agent List** (https\://a2aagentlist.com/) is a curated directory of A2A-compatible agents with a strong concentration of agents built on **OpenClaw** (an open-source AI agent framework with native A2A integration) and x402 V2 micropayment rails (USDC on Base, SKALE Europa gasless, and Arbitrum One)41. Crawling a2aagentlist.com yields rich multi-skill Agent Cards supporting streaming and push notifications, such as **OpSpawn AI Agent** (screenshot capture, PDF/HTML conversion, code security scanning, dependency vulnerability auditing), **PolicyCheck by LegalEasy** (pre-purchase e-commerce return/shipping/warranty policy risk assessment), **The Operator by Berlin AI Labs** (implementing the Proof of Execution PoE-A2A protocol extension for cryptographic verification), and **Brain AInstein** (multi-skill OpenClaw assistant with PriceHawk and SkillGuard)41.

### **6\. tiny.place (TinyHumans Identity & A2A Marketplace Directory)**

Documented at https\://tinyhumans.gitbook.io/tiny.place/discovery/directory, the **Tiny.place Directory** indexes individual A2A Agent Cards alongside agent collectives (Group) and tradable @handle identities11. To appear in the directory, every agent must publish a valid JSON Agent Card following the A2A schema with at least one declared skill and explicit paymentMethods ({network, asset} pairs)11. Crawling Tiny.place records yields base A2A Agent Cards enriched with @handle / cryptoId keys, per-skill inputSchema and pricing, social attestations (such as verified Twitter handles), and aggregate reputation scores (score, reviewCount, averageRating)11.

### **7\. a2aregistry.in (A2A Protocol Implementation Registry)**

Maintained by Heet Vekariya (https\://a2aregistry.in/), this community portal is designed to track official implementations, open-source projects, and tools/frameworks17. While its live counter in the captured page shows 0 registered implementations, it can be monitored as a low-frequency polling target for future community submissions10.

## **3\. Recursive Crawling: The 114 A2A Meta-Directories ("Directories of Directories")**

One of the most actionable structural findings from the a2aregistry.org sweep is that **114 out of 690 live A2A agents (16.5%) are categorized under Agent directories**30. Instead of merely indexing these 114 cards as terminal nodes, your crawler should treat them as **second-stage discovery hubs**: by sending A2A message/send requests to their /a2a endpoints or calling their /mcp servers, you can extract vertical and marketplace Agent Cards that are not listed in top-level registries12.

| Meta-Directory / Hub Name | Canonical Card URI & A2A Endpoint | Protocol Version | Programmatic Harvesting Mechanism (skills / MCP) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |

## **4\. On-Chain Smart Contract Registries and Web3 Indexers (ERC-8004)**

In August 2025, authors from MetaMask (Marco De Rossi), the Ethereum Foundation (Davide Crapis), Google (Jordan Ellis), and Coinbase (Erik Reppel) introduced **ERC-8004 (Trustless Agents)** (eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8004, PR \#1170) as an on-chain identity, reputation, and validation extension for Google's A2A protocol6. By Q2 2026, community trackers reported a growing set of agent identities registered across canonical deployments on Ethereum Mainnet, Arbitrum, Base, and Monad, frequently pairing A2A messaging with x402 stablecoin settlement rails9.  
ERC-8004 defines three lightweight smart contract registries: the **Identity Registry** (AgentRegistry.sol), **Reputation Registry**, and **Validation Registry**25. For an Agent Card crawler, the Identity Registry provides three concrete harvesting mechanisms:

> 1. **Direct Smart Contract Event Scraping (register & setAgentURI)**: Every agent registering under ERC-8004 mints an ERC-721 NFT (with URIStorage) in the singleton Identity Registry contract on its respective EVM chain ({namespace}:{chainId}:{identityRegistry}, e.g., eip155:1:0x742...)6. Calling register(string agentURI, MetadataEntry\[\] metadata), register(string agentURI), or setAgentURI(string agentURI) (or prototype registerAgent(address agent, string calldata agentURI)) emits on-chain registration events containing the agentURI13. The agentURI supports https\://, ipfs://, or inline data:application/json;base64,... strings and resolves to a registration file (type: "https\://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8004\#registration-v1") whose services\[\] array explicitly advertises the agent's A2A Agent Card URL, MCP endpoint, OASF record, ENS name, DID, and reserved agentWallet (verified via EIP-712 / ERC-1271 signatures)13. Additionally, agents verify HTTPS domain ownership by hosting https\://{endpoint-domain}/.well-known/agent-registration.json13.  
> 2. **Scraping Dedicated ERC-8004 Web3 Indexers**: Instead of running custom EVM event listeners across Ethereum Mainnet, Arbitrum, Base, and Monad, you can point your crawlers directly at the three specialized ERC-8004 explorers documented in the Monad developer guides—specifically **https\://www\.8004scan.io**, **https\://agentscan.info**, and **https\://8004agents.ai**—which already index on-chain Identity Registry tokens and off-chain Agent Cards6.  
> 3. **Programmatic Querying via agent0 SDK and Companion ERCs**: The ERC-8004 ecosystem maintains the **agent0 SDK** (available in TypeScript and Python), which provides built-in client methods to query the Identity, Reputation (giveFeedback, readAllFeedback, getSummary), and Validation (validationRequest, validationResponse, getAgentValidations) Registries across supported EVM networks9. You should also monitor emerging companion proposals on Ethereum Magicians, including **Trustless Agents Plus (TAP)** (a hub for fragmented ERC-8004 agents), **ERC-8126** (AI Agent Verification), **ERC-8240**, **ERC-8412**, and **ERC-8196**46.

## **5\. Decentralized, Federated, and DNS-Based Discovery Layers**

Beyond centralized web registries and EVM blockchains, a wave of IETF, Linux Foundation, MIT, and OWASP specifications have established federated DHTs, OCI container registries, local mDNS broadcasts, and unicast DNS resource records that directly advertise or resolve A2A Agent Cards.

### **1\. Linux Foundation AGNTCY: Agent Directory Service (dir) and OASF**

Welcomed by the Linux Foundation on July 29, 2025, **AGNTCY** (agntcy.org, docs.agntcy.org) builds open-source discovery, identity, and messaging infrastructure for multi-agent systems5. Its discovery layer pairs the **Open Agentic Schema Framework (OASF)** (latest release OASF v1.1.0 on July 10, 2026; github.com/agntcy/oasf, live schema server at schema.oasf.outshift.com and Protobuf definitions at buf.build/agntcy/oasf) with the **Agent Directory Service (ADS / dir)** (github.com/agntcy/dir, container images ghcr.io/agntcy/dir-apiserver:v1.9.0 and dir-ctl:v1.9.0, formalized in IETF draft draft-mp-agntcy-ads-03 and arXiv:2509.18787)5. OASF annotates A2A Agent Cards and MCP server listings with standardized taxonomy skills and domains without replacing the underlying A2A AgentCard JSON format, while ADS stores and routes records using **Open Container Initiative (OCI) registry infrastructure** (such as Zot) and content-addressed Distributed Hash Tables (DHTs)5. To crawl AGNTCY ADS, start a local node (dirctl daemon start listening on localhost:8888) or use the AGNTCY Directory client SDKs (Go, Python, .NET, Java/Kotlin, JS/TS) to connect to federated ADS peers (build/agntcy/dir) and resolve A2A Agent Cards by skill taxonomy, filtering on cryptographic verification flags (IsSigned, IsTrusted) and immutable ownership annotations (agntcy.dir/identity and agntcy.dir/owner)5.

### **2\. MIT Media Lab NANDA Quilt Registry and Verified AgentFacts**

Developed at the MIT Media Lab under Professor Ramesh Raskar (https\://www\.media.mit.edu/projects/mit-nanda/overview/, github.com/aidecentralized/NANDA-Quilt-of-Registries-and-Verified-AgentFacts, and IETF draft draft-raskar-agentic-web-federated-resolution-01), the **NANDA** project operates a federated "Quilt" of registries designed to scale to billions of autonomous agents13. NANDA separates discovery into a **two-step resolution flow**:

> 1. **Lean Reference Registry (![][image3] per record)**: Stores only static routing data—the canonical agentId, credential pointers, and dynamic FactsURL / PrivateFactsURL links—reducing registry write frequency by ![][image4] compared to DNS13.  
> 2. **Verified AgentFacts (JSON-LD)**: Resolving the FactsURL returns a cryptographically signed JSON-LD service manifest (AgentFacts) containing live endpoints, explicit resolution TTLs (1–6 hours static or sub-minute dynamic), capabilities, skills, Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) hashes, and short-lived W3C Verifiable Credentials (![][image5])13. For publishers without DNS control (such as SMBs or personal agents), **NandaIndex** (draft-raskar-agentic-web-federated-resolution-01) binds a Subject Identity directly to a terminal A2A Agent Card (artifact) or authorized gateway inside a standard AI Catalog response envelope13. Because AGNTCY's Agent Directory Service is explicitly designed to interoperate with the NANDA index, crawlers integrating NANDA SDKs and AGNTCY directory nodes can traverse agent records across both ecosystems70.

### **3\. GoDaddy ANS (Agent Name Service v1/v2) and ARD (Agentic Resource Discovery)**

To support domain-based identity verification and dynamic runtime discovery, GoDaddy and industry collaborators—including Cisco, Databricks, GitHub, Google, Hugging Face, Microsoft, Nvidia, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Snowflake, and OWASP—developed two complementary open specifications13. **ARD (https\://agenticresourcediscovery.org, github.com/ards-project/ard-spec v0.91)** standardizes dynamic, intent-based discovery of A2A agents, MCP servers, and ANS-registered resources, while **ANS (http\://ansinfo.ai, https\://www\.godaddy.com/ans, IETF draft-narajala-courtney-ansv2-02, and OWASP ANS v1.0)** (also introduced in arXiv:2505.10609) serves as the domain-based verifiable identity layer5.

* **Crawling the GoDaddy Agent Identity Portal & SDKs**: You can query GoDaddy's public registry at https\://www\.godaddy.com/ans (filtering directly by Protocol \= A2A, Tags, Transport Methods, and Capabilities) or integrate the open-source ANS SDKs in **Go** (github.com/godaddy/ans-sdk-go and reference implementation github.com/agentnameservice/ans), **Rust** (github.com/godaddy/ans-sdk-rust), and **Java** (github.com/godaddy/ans-sdk-java)5.  
* **Inspecting ANS DNS & Transparency Log Records**: Every ANS-registered agent receives a versioned ANSName (ans://v{version}.{agentHost}), a public TLS server certificate, a private identity certificate, and an immutable entry in a C2SP Merkle-tree **Transparency Log** (tlog-checkpoint and tlog-tiles at transparency.ans.godaddy.com)13. Crawlers can resolve ANS agents via DNS HTTPS/SVCB service binding records (v=ans1; version=1.2.0; protocols=mcp,a2a) and verify their status via \_ans-badge.{agentHost} (v=ans-badge1; version=v{version}; url={badgeURL}) or \_ra-badge DNS TXT records13.

### **4\. Local Link mDNS / DNS-SD Discovery (\_a2a.\_tcp.local. & \_agents.\_tcp)**

When crawling inside local networks, developer testbeds, smart buildings, or Kubernetes clusters where agents spin up with dynamic IPs, two IETF Internet-Drafts define zero-configuration Multicast DNS (mDNS, RFC 6762\) and DNS-Based Service Discovery (DNS-SD, RFC 6763\) profiles for A2A:

> 1. **draft-zhao-a2a-dns-sd-00 (\_a2a.\_tcp.local.)**: Triggered by A2A GitHub Issue \#378 (a2aproject/A2A\#378), this specification instructs A2A servers to advertise service type **\_a2a.\_tcp.local.** on the TCP port serving the Agent Card8. A local crawler browses PTR records for \_a2a.\_tcp.local., resolves the SRV target (host:port) and A/AAAA records, and parses four standardized TXT record keys: **card** (path to the Agent Card, defaulting to /.well-known/agent-card.json), **proto** (protocol binding, e.g., jsonrpc), **v** (A2A version, e.g., 1.0), and **tls** (1 for https, else http)8.  
> 2. **draft-jakab-dawn-agent-discovery-mdns-01 (\_agents.\_tcp with \_a2a subtype)**: Authored by Cisco Systems for the IETF DAWN working group (and adopted by projects like OpenClaw), this two-stage model uses the unified service type **\_agents.\_tcp** with per-protocol subtype **\_a2a** (\_a2a.\_sub.\_agents.\_tcp.local.) and publishes Minimum Discoverable Information (MDI) in TXT keys (desc-ref, title, proto-ver) before fetching the full AgentCard in Stage 213.

### **5\. Global Unicast DNS Discovery Standards (NAIS, AID, DAN, ADP/DNS-AID, and DAWN)**

For internet-wide DNS enumeration prior to HTTP probing, your DNS reconnaissance pipeline should query five emerging DNS record profiles:

| DNS Standard / IETF Draft | DNS Record Type & Node Name | Record Format / SvcParams | How Crawlers Use It to Locate A2A Cards |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **NAIS & AID v1.2/v2** (github.com/nais-standard/spec, draft-nemethi-aid-agent-identity-discovery) | TXT at \_agent.\<domain\> | Contains service endpoint URI, protocol token (a2a / mcp), and auth hint2. | Fast DNS TXT pre-check on any domain to confirm an active agent and extract its endpoint URI before sending HTTP GET requests2. |
| **ADP v1.1 \+ DNS-AID** (draft-pro-adp-agent-discovery-02 & draft-mozleywilliams-dnsop-dnsaid) | SVCB (RFC 9460\) \+ TLSA (DANE) at agent FQDN (fallback: TXT \+ SRV) | alpn="a2a,h2,h3", bap="a2a", well-known="agent.json", cap="https\://...", cap-sha256="..."13. | Resolves connectivity, A2A protocol support (bap=a2a), and exact well-known card path in a single DNS round trip13. |
| **DAN (DNS-Based Agent Naming)** (draft-seethiraju-dawn-dan-01, Verisign) | AIINDEX and AIDISCA RR types (DNSSEC-signed) | AIINDEX lists all published agent names in a zone; AIDISCA binds protocol, coarse capability, endpoint, and X.509 cert13. | Querying AIINDEX on a domain zone enumerates all sub-agent publication names without brute-forcing subdomains13. |
| **DAWN DNS-like Architecture** (draft-yao-dawn-agent-discovery-architect-01, CNNIC / Huawei / China Mobile) | A, SVCB, SRV at \<prefix\>.\<suffix\> Composite FQDN; local resolver at \_agent-index.\_tcp | Maps composite FQDNs (e.g., agent-hotel.example.example-registry1.com) to fixed JSON Capability Cards (capability\_list, network\_endpoint)13. | Discover local Agent Resolvers via \_agent-index.\_tcp or synchronize zone transfers from whitelisted Agent Registries13. |
| **ANP Agent Name System** (draft-song-anp-ans-00) | DHT \+ GossipSub \+ DNS SRV/TXT | Maps agent:// URIs via AITP methods (ans.register, ans.resolve, ans.lookup) and /.well-known/agent-card.json13. | Query ans.lookup across ANP DHT nodes to resolve peer identifiers and capability descriptors13. |

Auto-ingests /.well-known/agent-card.json from Vertex AI Agent Engine (client.agent\_engines.create), Cloud Run (--functional-type=agent \--identity-type=agent-identity), and GKE pods (registry.gke.io/functional-type: "AGENT" \+ a2a-protocol.org/agent-card annotation)12. Query with roles/agentregistry.viewer using boolean operators (AND, OR, NOT) or prefix wildcards (displayName:Best\_A2A\_\*) across management boundaries12. |

Stores A2A cards in descriptors.a2aAgentCard.data with schema version in descriptors.a2aAgentCard.dataSchemaVersion (validating against \#/definitions/AgentCard v0.3). ## **8\. Crawler Engineering Playbook: Parsing, Verification, and Security Defenses**

Once your crawlers begin ingesting JSON payloads from the sources above, your ingestion pipeline should implement seven validation, security, and corroboration controls tailored to the 2026 A2A ecosystem:

> 1. **Reject HTML and SPA Fallbacks at .well-known Paths**: Many web servers return HTTP 200 OK with an HTML login screen or Single-Page Application (SPA) fallback bundle when a crawler requests /.well-known/agent-card.json1. Enforce strict Content-Type: application/json (or application/a2a+json) validation and structural JSON checks before indexing1.  
> 2. **Support Dual-Schema Parsing (A2A v0.3 vs. v1.0.0) and Non-Strict Cards**: Although A2A v1.0.0 reached stability in March 2026, a large proportion of live agents on a2aregistry.org as of November 2026 still publish v0.3.0 cards4. In v0.3, the service endpoint and protocol version sit at the top level ("url": "https\://...", "protocolVersion": "0.3.0") and capabilities include "stateTransitionHistory"2. In v1.0.0, top-level url and protocolVersion are deprecated and replaced by "supportedInterfaces": \[{"url": "...", "protocolBinding": "HTTP+JSON" \| "JSONRPC" \| "GRPC", "protocolVersion": "1.0", "tenant": "..."}\] ordered by preference1. Moreover, because 55 of the 65 domain cards found in the July 2026 API Evangelist scan were not strictly conformant (for example, Cloudflare's card omits version and defaultInputModes and points skill endpoint fields to /llms.txt and /{path}.md, while www\.a2a-registry.org's agents.json schema uses input\_schema inside capabilities instead of skills), your crawler should store raw JSON alongside normalized fields rather than dropping non-strict cards40.  
> 3. **Handle Hybrid Cloud Runtime Cards and System Prompt Leakage (AWS Bedrock AgentCore)**: Field-by-field cross-cloud testing (github.com/xbill9/multicloud-agentcard) revealed three critical quirks when crawling AWS Bedrock AgentCore cards compared to Google Cloud Run and Azure Container Apps28:  
   * **Hybrid v0.3 \+ v1.0 Structure**: AgentCore cards declare "protocolVersion": "0.3" and top-level "url" / "preferredTransport" while simultaneously carrying the v1.0 "supportedInterfaces" array28. Your parser must inspect supportedInterfaces even when top-level protocolVersion claims 0.328.  
   * **Sub-Path Discovery & Session Headers**: AgentCore cards do not sit at a hostname root; they sit beneath /runtimes/{escaped\_arn}/invocations/.well-known/agent-card.json and require both the X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id header and the AWS IAM GetAgentCard permission (an IAM policy with only InvokeAgentRuntime will reject card fetches)28.  
   * **System Prompt & Model ID Exposure**: By default, the a2a-sdk card builder on Strands/AgentCore populates skills\[\].description with the agent's **entire system prompt** (e.g., 1,258 characters of internal instructions, bloating the card to 2,109 bytes—![][image6] larger than Cloud Run) and places the underlying LLM model ID in skills\[\].tags28. Crawlers can mine skills\[\].description and tags to fingerprint underlying foundation models and system prompts across deployed Strands agents28.  
> 4. **Verify JWS Signatures (RFC 8785 \+ RFC 7515\)**: Production A2A v1.0 cards may include a "signatures" array containing JSON Web Signatures (typ: "JOSE", alg, kid, and optional jku JWKS URL in the base64url protected header)1. To verify signature integrity, your crawler must remove fields holding default values (unless required or marked optional, such as removing empty extensions: \[\]), exclude the signatures field itself, canonicalize the JSON per RFC 8785 (JCS), and verify against the publisher's JWKS (supported via verifyAgentCardSignature and canonicalizeAgentCard in @a2a-js/sdk)1.  
> 5. **Distinguish Static Card Validity from Live task\_conformance (and Structured Input Requirements)**: As demonstrated by a2aregistry.org, a card can pass JSON schema validation while its declared endpoint returns 404 Not Found (e.g., Agent Contract Proof), 401 Unauthorized on POST (e.g., AgentNet), or an unwrapped Task object instead of a v1.0 SendMessageResponse (e.g., BerrerGate)7. Conversely, some valid agents (such as MyDankTank) reject plain-text probe messages with \-32602 Invalid params because they strictly require structured JSON DataPart inputs ({"skill": "...", "params": {...}})19. Your active prober should test a plain-text TextPart first and fall back to a structured DataPart payload matching a declared skill ID before marking an agent non-conformant19.  
> 6. **Implement Multi-Source Corroboration Across Network Vantages (draft-chandra-agent-registry-corroboration-01)**: A single registry or directory can misrepresent an agent via **omission** (withholding a record) or **equivocation** (serving different signed cards to different observers)13. Following IETF draft-chandra-agent-registry-corroboration-01, high-assurance crawlers should resolve target agents across multiple independent sources and network vantages (region:us, region:eu, asn:as64500), canonicalize claims via RFC 8785 (CORR-DIGEST), and flag omission, source\_equivocation, or scope\_violation discrepancies13.  
> 7. **Sanitize Card Fields Against Prompt Injection and Typosquatting**: Both the official a2a-samples disclaimer and security researchers (AuthZed) warn that external Agent Cards must be treated as untrusted inputs4. Malicious actors can embed adversarial prompt-injection payloads inside name, description, or skills\[\].description—or register typosquatted agent cards—to hijack downstream orchestrator LLMs when card text is injected into prompts3. Always sanitize third-party card strings, isolate them from system instructions, and cross-check publisher authenticity via JWS signatures, GoDaddy ANS badges, DNS verification, or ERC-8004 reputation histories before routing live tasks1.

### **Field-by-Field Amalgamation & Normalization Matrix**

| JSON Field / Path | Specification / Dialect Origin | Status & Cardinality | Crawler Normalization & Parsing Rule |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| name, description, version | A2A v0.2.4, v0.3.0, v1.0.0, agents.json | Required across all specs (though version is omitted by non-strict cards like Cloudflare)1. | Index name and description for full-text search; default version to "0.0.0" if missing2. Check description length (![][image7]) for leaked system prompts28. |
| supportedInterfaces\[\] (url, protocolBinding, protocolVersion, tenant) | Official A2A v1.0.0 Specification | Required in v1.0; present on hybrid v0.3 cards (Bedrock AgentCore)1. | Primary routing array ordered by preference1. Extract url, protocolBinding (JSONRPC, HTTP+JSON, GRPC), protocolVersion, and optional multi-tenant tenant ID1. |
| url & protocolVersion (top-level) | A2A v0.2.4 & v0.3.0 (Deprecated in v1.0.0) | Required in v0.3; deprecated at top level in v1.03. | If supportedInterfaces is absent, synthesize supportedInterfaces\[0\] from top-level url, protocolVersion (default "0.3.0"), and preferredTransport (default "JSONRPC")3. |
| preferredTransport / preferred\_transport & additional\_interfaces | A2A v0.3.0, Bedrock AgentCore, & AgentScope Runtime (AgentCardWithRuntimeConfig) | Optional legacy / framework transport hints28. | Map preferredTransport / preferred\_transport and additional\_interfaces into normalized transport bindings when parsing v0.3 or AgentScope cards28. |
| capabilities.streaming & capabilities.pushNotifications | A2A v0.3.0 & v1.0.0 | Optional booleans (default false)1. | Indicates support for SendStreamingMessage (SSE/gRPC) and webhook TaskPushNotificationConfig1. |
| capabilities.extendedAgentCard vs. supportsAuthenticatedExtendedCard | A2A v1.0.0 vs. A2A v0.3.0 | Optional boolean1. | Normalize both flags to a single has\_extended\_card boolean; triggers secondary fetch via GetExtendedAgentCard1. |
| capabilities.stateTransitionHistory | A2A v0.3.0 & Cloudflare Card | Optional boolean in v0.32. | Preserved for backward compatibility with v0.3 state tracking3. |
| capabilities.extensions\[\] | A2A v1.0.0 Extension Mechanism | Optional array of {uri, params} objects1. | Inspect uri to detect **Agent Galaxy claims** (https\://agentgalaxy.dev/extensions/claim/v1), **LangGraph history scope**, **a2a-x402 crypto payments**, or **Proof of Execution (PoE-A2A)**16. |
| defaultInputModes\[\] & defaultOutputModes\[\] | A2A v0.3.0 & v1.0.0 \+ LangGraph A2UI | Required in v1.0 (e.g., \["text/plain", "application/json"\])1. | Check for application/json+a2ui or application/a2ui+json to identify agents capable of streaming generative UI (A2UI) components16. |
| skills\[\] (id, name, description, tags, examples, inputModes, outputModes) | A2A v0.3.0 & v1.0.0 | Required array in standard A2A cards1. | Core capability index3. Also parse non-standard extensions inside skills\[\]: endpoint (used by Cloudflare for /llms.txt), inputSchema / price (used by tiny.place), and capabilities\[\].input\_schema (used by agents.json)2. |
| securitySchemes, securityRequirements, security, authentication | A2A v1.0 (securitySchemes \+ securityRequirements), A2A JS (security), agents.json (authentication) | Optional security declarations1. | Supports 5 standard types in v1.0 (apiKey, http, oauth2, openIdConnect, mutualTLS)1. Normalize legacy security and authentication objects into unified auth metadata14. |
| signatures\[\] (protected, signature, header) | A2A v1.0.0 JWS Signing (RFC 8785 \+ RFC 7515\) | Optional array of JWS signatures1. | Canonicalize card per RFC 8785 (stripping default values and signatures) and verify against kid / jku JWKS1. |
| paymentMethods\[\], x402Support, registrations\[\], annotations | Tiny.place, www\.a2a-registry.org, ERC-8004, & AGNTCY OASF | Ecosystem commerce & identity extensions5. | Tracks autonomous settlement rails (USDC on Base eip155:8453, Solana, Polygon, Arbitrum, SKALE via x402), on-chain ERC-721 agentId bindings, and OASF CID ownership5. |
